plan.title: Psoriasis lesional vs control hallmark pathway enrichment
plan.analytical_narrative: The DESeq2 differential expression for the treated (psoriasis lesional) vs control skin contrast is already delivered (de_results.csv, 12000 genes, 6 vs 6 unpaired). The research question asks only which hallmark pathways change, so no new differential test is fitted. First, a sample-structure QC step on the raw counts confirms the design is sound and flags the known low-depth sample (sample_01, ~4x below median library size) before its presence is treated as inherited context for the enrichment. Second, a preranked GSEA (fgsea) is run on the full ranked gene list from the delivered DESeq2 results against the MSigDB Hallmark human collection (50 sets), the primary pass per the applicable procedure, followed by Reactome and WikiPathways human collections as secondary passes for pathway-level resolution of any hallmark hit. Genes are ranked by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the 'stat' column), the disputed-but-defensible default that scales effect size by its uncertainty; the plan states this choice explicitly per the ranking-metric rule. A report step consolidates the enrichment results with the required reproducibility and methodological disclosures (gene set database versions, ranking metric, universe, size window, leading-edge genes, method-dependence caveat).

flags.message: If fewer than about 50 genes pass the significance threshold, do not run an over-representation test on that list. A hypergeometric test of a short list finds no category, and a change of the threshold changes the list and the result. Run the ranked method on the full list of tested genes instead, because it finds a set of genes with a small but coordinated change that no single gene shows. State the size of the significant list in the report.
